lessons.title: Non-Fiction: Amazing Plants
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about plants from a non-fiction text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about a plant.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a simple non-fiction text about unusual plants around the world.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions about plants.
key_questions: What is special about this plant?
Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Find a fact about a plant at home.

lessons.title: Counting Plants and Petals
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count sets of plant-themed objects to 20.
success_criteria: I can count petals on a flower.
I can write the numeral.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model counting petals/leaves on plant pictures, recording numerals.
lessons.independent_task: Children count plant-themed counters/pictures up to 20, recording numerals.
key_questions: How many petals does this flower have?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting accuracy — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.home_link: Count petals on a flower at home or in a picture.

lessons.title: Plants Around the World
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how plants differ in different climates.
success_criteria: I can name a plant from a hot place.
I can name a plant from a cold place.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap hot/cold places from last week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss how plants like cacti suit hot dry places, and evergreens suit cold places.
lessons.independent_task: Children match plants to their climate, recording their reasoning.
key_questions: Why does a cactus store water?
Why do evergreens keep their leaves in winter?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain adaptation reasoning for each plant

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of plant adaptation to climate — evidence for SCI.PLA.
lessons.home_link: Look up an unusual plant together.

lessons.title: Writing About My Favourite Plant
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write descriptive sentences about a plant.
success_criteria: I can describe a plant.
I can write a full sentence.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing descriptive sentences about a plant.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 sentences describing their favourite plant from the week's learning.
key_questions: What does this plant look like?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive writing progress — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Describe a plant to your family.

lessons.title: Measuring Plant Height
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to measure and compare plant heights using non-standard units.
success_criteria: I can measure a plant's height.
I can compare two plant heights.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model measuring plant picture heights using cubes.
lessons.independent_task: Children measure and compare plant picture heights using linking cubes.
resources_needed: Plant picture cards of varying heights
key_questions: How many cubes tall is this plant?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record height measurement consolidation — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Measure a plant at home using cubes or hand spans.

lessons.title: Trees: Deciduous and Evergreen
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to distinguish between deciduous and evergreen trees.
success_criteria: I can say what deciduous means.
I can name an evergreen tree.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what happens to some trees in autumn/winter.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss the difference between deciduous trees (lose leaves) and evergreen trees (keep leaves).
lessons.independent_task: Children sort tree picture cards into deciduous/evergreen, recording reasoning.
key_questions: Does this tree lose its leaves?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain reasoning for less obvious examples

lessons.assessment_notes: Note plant classification understanding — evidence for SCI.PLA.
lessons.home_link: Look at trees near your home — are they deciduous or evergreen?

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Plant Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read plant-themed words.
success_criteria: I can blend and read plant words.
I can read a sentence about plants.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending plant-themed words (e.g. 'leaf', 'tree', 'root').
lessons.independent_task: Children read plant-themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading plant words over the week.

lessons.title: Fractions Recap: Halves of Leaves
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to find half of plant-themed shapes and quantities.
success_criteria: I can find half of a leaf shape.
I can find half of a quantity of plants.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model finding half of leaf shapes (folding) and plant quantities.
lessons.independent_task: Children find half of given leaf shapes and quantities.
key_questions: What is half of this leaf?
What is half of this many plants?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record fraction consolidation — evidence for MATHS.N4.
lessons.home_link: Find half of a group of objects at home.

lessons.title: Wild vs Garden Plants
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to distinguish between wild and garden plants.
success_criteria: I can name a wild plant.
I can name a garden plant.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss plants seen growing wild vs in gardens.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss the difference between wild plants (grow without help) and garden plants (planted/cared for).
lessons.independent_task: Children sort plant picture cards into wild/garden, recording reasoning.
resources_needed: Wild and garden plant picture cards
key_questions: Is this plant wild or in a garden?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note plant classification understanding — evidence for SCI.PLA.
lessons.home_link: Spot a wild plant and a garden plant near your home.

lessons.title: Plant Riddles
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe a plant clearly enough for others to guess it.
success_criteria: I can give 3 clues about my plant.
I can guess a friend's plant.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult models a riddle about a plant.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss how to give clear clues without naming the plant.
lessons.independent_task: Children create and share plant riddles in pairs, guessing each other's.

differentiation.support: Use picture cards to prompt clues

lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive spoken language skill — evidence for ENG.SL1.
lessons.plenary: Share favourite riddles with the class.
lessons.home_link: Make up a plant riddle for your family.

lessons.title: Plant Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction word problems using a plant context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using a plant context (e.g. flowers picked/planted).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve plant-themed word problems, showing working.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a plant word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Famous Plants and Their Uses
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe a use for a well-known plant.
success_criteria: I can name a plant and its use.
I can say why it's useful.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss useful plants around the world (rice, wheat, cotton, rubber trees) and their uses.
lessons.independent_task: Children match plants to their uses, recording their matching.
key_questions: What is this plant used for?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of plants' usefulness to humans — evidence for SCI.PLA.
lessons.home_link: Find something at home made from a plant (cotton, wood, paper).

lessons.title: Plants Around the World Quiz
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about plants around the world.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about world plants, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: Why does a cactus have spines instead of leaves?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on plant facts you learned.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Fractions and Measuring
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply fraction and measuring skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can find half of something.
I can measure and compare height.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of halves and measuring height.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: fractions, measuring.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 30 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N4/MEA.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising fractions over the weekend.

lessons.title: Plants Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about plants around the world.
success_criteria: I can name a plant and where it grows.
I can name a use for a plant.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering climate adaptation, tree types, wild/garden plants, and plant uses.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a class 'Plants Around the World' display.
key_questions: What have we learned about plants?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: Note plant understanding progress — evidence for SCI.PLA.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about plants with your family.
